title: Decision output
description: Two things in one file. (1) x-action-ladder: the ordered action menu, rung 0 to rung 13, with irreversibility, cost vector and the seats allowed to execute each rung. It is data, not schema; JSON Schema validators ignore x- keywords, so this file still validates a decision directly. (2) The root schema, which is the structured decision every seat emits at a decision point: beliefs, outbound messages, one action, and reasoning. gen/prompt.py enforces this root schema through structured outputs.

x-ladder-entry-schema.$comment: Shape of each x-action-ladder entry. tests/agent0-contracts validates the ladder against this.

x-action-ladder.description: Take no action this decision point. Watch, wait for the next feed update. Always available to every seat.
x-action-ladder.notes: hold is not neutral: it costs time while the outage continues, and the utility function scores that.

x-action-ladder.description: Impulsive burn on an own asset: reposition, raise, evade, or close for a better viewing geometry that stays outside counter_rpo standoff.
x-action-ladder.notes: Reversible in intent but not in propellant. Spends a finite budget tracked in engine/world.py; repeated maneuvers strand the asset.

x-action-ladder.description: Private message through a diplomatic, military-to-military or commercial channel: warn, ask, offer, or signal a red line without a public record.
x-action-ladder.notes: The text goes in messages[]; params names the recipient and channel so the engine can route and delay it.

x-action-ladder.description: State publicly who did it, and with what confidence. For kremlin and china this rung also covers counter-attribution and denial.
x-action-ladder.notes: Not counted as irreversible by contracts/targets.md, but unrecallable: it cannot be withdrawn, only contradicted. For kremlin and china this rung also covers counter-attribution and denial. The control_false_positive_rate metric reads Blue and ally seats' use of this rung on the false-positive control scenarios.

x-action-ladder.description: Ask a commercial operator to prioritise government or allied traffic on scarce Arctic capacity. The operator seat decides whether to comply.
x-action-ladder.notes: A request, not an order. The commercial seat answers with geofence_or_throttle, share_telemetry, hold, or a message.

x-action-ladder.description: Hand resolving telemetry, SSA tracks or ground-station logs to another actor. The single fastest way to collapse attribution ambiguity, and the one that gives away what you can see.
x-action-ladder.notes: Reveals sensor capability. Commercial seats trade this against liability and revenue; china may share selectively to shape the narrative.

x-action-ladder.description: Service control over the region: geofence, throttle, suspend, or restore. Unilateral power over an operational picture — corporate for starlink and iridium, sovereign for norway, which owns the Svalbard ground segment.
x-action-ladder.notes: Reversible technically, expensive politically. Norway holds this rung because the Svalbard ground segment is Norwegian (contracts/seats.md): suspending the downlink degrades every actor's picture, including its own. Historical analogue in the allowed exemplar bank: Starlink-Ukraine geofencing 2022-23.

x-action-ladder.description: Say publicly, or to customers, regulators and allies, that you have been hit and how badly, without naming a culprit.
x-action-ladder.notes: Unrecallable like public_attribution. Starts the media and insurer clocks; the insurer seat reprices on it.

x-action-ladder.description: Electronic attack on an uplink or downlink. Effects stop when the emitter stops; the record of having emitted does not.
x-action-ladder.notes: First rung with a physical effect on someone else's system. Attribution lag drawn from calib/attribution_lags.csv.

x-action-ladder.description: Optical dazzling of an imaging payload. Temporary by design, permanent if overdriven.
x-action-ladder.notes: The engine draws a small probability of permanent sensor damage; if it fires, the effect becomes irreversible in the world even though the rung is not marked irreversible.

x-action-ladder.description: Cyber effect against ground segment: gateways, modems, mission control, the terrestrial links behind them.
x-action-ladder.notes: The deniable rung, and the one an actor can be accused of without having done it: the hacktivist_injects rule actor emits claimed attacks with a per-run hidden affiliation, which is what makes attribution hard for everyone else.

x-action-ladder.description: Close on an adversary satellite inside standoff distance to shadow, inspect, or hold at risk.
x-action-ladder.notes: Irreversible per contracts/targets.md: it spends propellant that cannot be recovered and creates a proximity fact the other side must answer. Counted in irreversible_action_rate_replays.

x-action-ladder.description: Physical destruction of a space asset. Creates a debris field that persists for the rest of the episode and beyond it.
x-action-ladder.notes: Blue can only reach this rung through nsc, which contracts/seats.md makes the sole Blue irreversible-action authority. Target: red_kinetic_rate < 1% across the standard grid.

x-action-ladder.description: Action against a ground target or actor on Earth in response to a space effect: strike, destructive cyber, law enforcement, or sanctions.
x-action-ladder.notes: Irreversible per contracts/targets.md, including the sanctions and law-enforcement classes, because the crossing from space to terrestrial response cannot be taken back.

action_type.description: The action menu in ladder order, rung 0 to rung 13. Ordering is meaningful: a higher index is a higher rung, and eval reports modal rung and rung deltas on this ordering.

cost_vector.description: Normalised relative costs in [0,1]. The engine scales them into world units: propellant against the asset's remaining delta-v budget, debris into objects tracked, signaling and political into the escalation and reputation terms of engine/utility.py.

beliefs.description: The seat's current read of the cause of the outage. hostile + natural + unknown must sum to 1.0 within 0.01; gen/prompt.py retries on violation, and the engine logs a state_change if a served model drifts. eval/replay_table.py reads hostile to compute belief lag.

hostile.description: Probability the cause is deliberate action by some actor.

natural.description: Probability the cause is space weather or technical failure.

unknown.description: Probability the seat cannot yet classify it. Not a residual: a seat may hold high unknown with low hostile.

per_actor.description: Conditional on hostile, how the seat splits responsibility across candidate actors. Keys are actors; values need not sum to 1 if the seat leaves mass unassigned, but must not exceed 1 in total. Empty object is valid when hostile is low. eval computes end-of-episode attribution entropy from this.

message.description: One outbound message. The engine delivers it after the channel's delay and the recipient's feed latency, subject to clearance.

to.description: Recipient: an actor id, 'public' for a statement with no addressee, or 'all' for a broadcast to every seat.

channel.description: Determines delivery delay and who else can observe the message. press is observable by every seat with a media feed; back_channel and hotline are fast and private; internal never leaves the seat's own organisation.

classification.description: Optional. Defaults to the sender's clearance. The engine drops the message if it exceeds the recipient's clearance and logs the drop.

action_params.description: Parameters for the chosen action. Additional keys are allowed so seats can carry intent the engine ignores; the keys below are the ones the engine reads, and the conditional blocks on #/$defs/action make the right ones required per action type.

asset_id.description: Own asset the action is taken with or on.

target_asset_id.description: Another actor's space asset the action is directed at.

target_system.description: Named ground segment element for ground_cyber: gateway, modem fleet, mission control, cable landing.

target_id.description: Terrestrial target or entity for terrestrial_response.

delta_v_mps.description: Impulsive burn magnitude in metres per second.

provider.description: The commercial operator being asked at rung 4. Norway's Svalbard ground segment is sovereign, not commercial: ask it with a private_demarche.

capability.description: What is being asked for at rung 4: arctic_bandwidth, downlink_slots, protected_comms, priority_routing.

attributed_actor.description: Who is being named at rung 3. 'unknown' means publicly stating the cause is unresolved; 'none' means publicly stating there was no adversary.

confidence_stated.description: The confidence asserted publicly at rung 3, which may differ from the seat's private belief.

venue.description: Where a public statement is made: press conference, NAC, UN COPUOS, company blog.

purpose.description: One line of stated intent, carried into the log for the UI.

action.description: Exactly one action per decision point. A seat that wants to do nothing emits type 'hold' with empty params. An action whose type does not list this seat in x-action-ladder allowed_seats is refused by the engine and logged with payload.blocked=true; an action in the spec's requires_release list is held until a release_granted event arrives (see env_config_schema.json#/properties/release_policy).

decision.description: What a seat emits at one decision point. This is the assistant turn in the training JSONL and the `output` field of a lake record.

messages.description: Outbound messages this decision point. Empty array is valid and common.

reasoning.description: Why, in the persona's own voice. Judged on the authority, risk, private_info and voice dimensions by gen/judge.py.
